title: Recapitulation: Summing Up All Things in Christ
aka: gather up all things in Christ
lead: The Greek verb anakephalaiosasthai (Ephesians 1:10) means to sum up, to gather under one head or main point. Paul says God's plan is to bring all things in heaven and earth together in Christ. Irenaeus of Lyon (about AD 180) built a whole teaching on the word: Christ goes over the story of Adam again and sets it right.

sections.b: The verb is built on kephalaion, the main point or sum of a matter, and sounds like kephale, "head". Paul uses it only twice: love "sums up" the commandments (Romans 13:9), and in Ephesians 1:10 God plans "to bring all things together in Christ." Readers have taken it as summing up (a total), as bringing under one head (a ruler), as renewing or restoring, or as all of these. Ephesians 1:22 speaks of Christ as head over all things, and Colossians 1:20 of the reconciling of all things.

Irenaeus, bishop of Lyon, wrote in Against Heresies (3.18; 3.21; 5.1) that Christ "recapitulated" humanity: he passes again through the stages of human life and undoes Adam's disobedience by his obedience (compare Romans 5:12-21). The idea became central in Eastern Christian teaching, where salvation is the healing and renewing of human nature, and it is one root of the doctrine of theosis.
